title: UniverseSelectionInput
description: The deterministic pre-filter's output and the ONLY thing the Universe Selector agent may see. Contains underlyings with evidence already retrieved, normalised and quality-assessed by the data layer - never a raw provider payload, never a broker handle, never an option contract. Every candidate here is already deterministically eligible; the agent ranks, it does not admit.

as_of.description: The instant the universe is reconstructed for. No evidence retrieved after this instant may appear anywhere below.

candidate_assets.description: Deterministically eligible underlyings. May be empty - an empty universe is a valid outcome.

deterministic_filter_config.description: The filter thresholds actually applied, echoed so a stored run explains itself without consulting the config tree it ran under.

data_snapshot_ids.description: Every immutable data snapshot this input was derived from.

candidate_asset.description: One underlying security. Never an option contract and never a strategy.

reference_price_field.description: Which quote field the reference price came from. A price whose origin is unrecorded cannot be audited.

underlying_volume.description: Underlying share volume for the CURRENT SESSION, verbatim from the broker. Deliberately NOT option liquidity - that needs option-level data this milestone does not collect. From IBKR's delayed feed this is tick 74, which is known to arrive corrupted; it is preserved and flagged, never rescaled, and the liquidity floor does not read it.

average_daily_volume.description: Trailing 90-day average daily share volume (IBKR tick 21 / avVolume, via generic tick 165). This is the field the deterministic liquidity floor evaluates. An independent observation, never derived from underlying_volume and never substituted by it. Still underlying liquidity, so still NOT evidence about option liquidity.

market_data_origin.description: null when no quote was available. An absent origin and a SIMULATED one are different claims.

data_quality_summary.description: The data layer's verdict, carried through verbatim. Eight independent dimensions, because a record can be well-formed and economically impossible at once.

provenance.description: Who actually produced the evidence, and when we had it.

nullable_money.description: Exact decimal as a string, or null for unavailable. Never a JSON number: binary floating point must not reach an accounting decision. null and 0 are different claims.
